iPhone Ultra is about to make its debut at the recently confirmed September 9 event. Apple's foldable phone arrives a full seven years later than other comparable products, but three key features of the iPhone Ultra are absolutely worth the wait. Here's a look at the highlights.

#1: A nearly crease-free display

Samsung's first foldable smartphone launched in 2019, a full seven years ahead of the iPhone Ultra. However, rumours suggest that one of Apple's goals in developing a foldable phone is to completely eliminate any visible crease on the screen.

The visible crease on the inner display has always been a design compromise for foldable phones. But all signs currently point to Apple successfully achieving its goal of a nearly crease-free screen.

According to leakers, at certain angles and lighting conditions, a faint crease may still be barely visible. But overall, we expect the unfolded inner display to look essentially completely free of creases.

#2: Ultra-thin, with battery life and performance to match

Foldable smartphones that aren't thin enough often end up feeling bulky. However, achieving thinness usually requires sacrifices in battery life, performance and thermal performance.

However, rumours suggest that last year's iPhone Air laid the groundwork in many ways for building an ultra-thin foldable iPhone, while also balancing battery life and performance.

The iPhone Ultra's battery life is not expected to be significantly longer than that of the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but thanks to the battery hardware specs, combined with the power efficiency improvements of the A20 Pro and C2 chips, the battery performance should still be quite impressive.

In addition, the A20 Pro paired with a vapour chamber cooling design will also deliver outstanding performance.

#3: A durable hinge, with over 15 years of R&D behind it

According to reports, the iPhone Ultra's hinge will use liquid metal. This technology was first licensed by the company some 15 years ago.

In the early 2010s, many predictions pointed out that liquid metal could help make the iPhone thinner and lighter. As early as 2010, there were even mentions of the technology being applied to Apple's foldable phone development.

Now we may finally see liquid metal come into its own. Reports indicate that this will help Apple create a hinge that is durable, smooth and able to withstand long-term frequent use.

Apple could absolutely have launched a foldable iPhone much earlier, but it seems now is the right time to release a foldable that meets the quality standards expected of an iPhone.
